title: the clearance gate's declaring() returns posix proof paths
intention: ClearanceGate.declaring returns forward-slash proof paths on every host, so the clearance crossing journals a posix proven_by.
why: Measured 2026-11-12 on akiendell: the PROVEME crossing of 703d3ec3619c journaled proven_by cairn\\tools\\base\\proofs\\test_a_crossing_proven_by_is_posix.py on Windows
traces_to: Law 7: a record of truth is written right at its writer, never repaired by readers; Law 3: measured on Windows.
how: In cairn/devices/codemother/machines/clearance/gate.py declaring() appends p.relative_to(repo).as_posix() for a repo proof and p.as_posix() for a commons one. Red-first proof cairn/devices/codemother/machines/clearance/proofs/test_declaring_returns_posix_paths.py builds a scratch repo with a proof under proofs/ declaring a ticket id, asks a ClearanceGate over scratch roots, and asserts the result holds no backslash and equals the posix path.

clauses.claim: declaring() over a scratch repo returns the proof as a forward-slash path with no backslash
the proof reds against the unedited gate.py, where the path came back with backslashes

decisions.text: D2: one proof, one tooth per clause; red first.
